answer: At a haven trading ferrous scrap recovered from the ocean, each bidding agent proves that its owner holds a live salvage permit without revealing the owner. The proof carries a permit nullifier: the auction accepts one subsidized bid per nullifier each epoch, even when many accounts present it. Fifty aliases cannot claim fifty subsidies unless the attacker obtains fifty permits, paying inspections, deposits and fees. Stolen permits and colluding inspectors remain risks, so the registry supports revocation and random dock audits; legitimate operators denied a permit need an appeal route.
